title: diffusive-reservation-allocator-and-catchup-backoff
author: Alyssa Chen
release_notes: Introduce a diffusive reservation allocator with a catchup-backoff reclaim policy and a compact utilization fingerprint metric. Improves stability of dedicated fleet reservations under bursty tenant patterns and reduces oscillation. Rollout behind feature flag; no API changes.
description: Context: some customers using Dedicated report frequent reservation churn and oscillation during mixed steady+bursty traffic patterns. Current per-tenant reservation adjustments are reactive and often create overcorrections that worsen tail latency or force expensive scaling. Motivation: reduce oscillation, improve fairness, and give the autoscaler a principled smoothing mechanism that preserves responsiveness for genuine demand spikes. Design summary: (1) Diffusive reservation allocator: a control-layer algorithm that treats reservation deltas as 'diffusive' quantities propagated across a tenant graph within a pool. Small reservation increases are spread proportionally to neighboring tenants' headroom to avoid single-tenant spikes monopolizing warming capacity. (2) Catchup-backoff reclaim: when utilization falls below a tenant's reservation, we enter a measured catchup window (configurable) before hard reclaim; reclaimed volume is staggered using a backoff curve to avoid sudden capacity returns that trigger downstream allocation churn. (3) Utilization fingerprint: lightweight per-tenant time-series sketching (exponentially-weighted buckets + quantile sketch) producing a 128-bit stable fingerprint used for telemetry comparison and regression detection. Implementation notes: allocator implemented in pkg/autoscaler/diffusive_allocator.go; control knobs surfaced in config/dedicated/autoscaler.yaml and feature-gated via dedicated.diffusive_reservations; telemetry hooks in pkg/telemetry/util_fingerprint.go; unit and simulation tests added in tests/autoscaler/*.py. Testing & results: simulator runs (10k synthetic tenants, mixed poisson+bursty arrivals) show 28% reduction in reservation churn events and 12% lower 95th-percentile latency variance under constrained capacity. Benchmarks on staging fleet (N=120 GPUs) confirm a 6% reduction in cold-starts for tenants exhibiting short spikes. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout: 5% of pools -> 25% -> 100% with observability gating (reservation_churn, p95_latency_variance, fairness_index). Safety: hard caps prevent diffusive spread from exceeding 15% of pool capacity; emergency disable switch added in console. Checklist: [x] design doc added (docs/design/diffusive-reservation.md) [x] unit tests [x] integration sim tests [x] bench runs attached [x] documented config knobs [x] canary rollout plan.

review_comments: Marco Silva: Nice approach. Concern: how do we bound the diffusion so a noisy tenant doesn't cannibalize pool? Please add a hard cap and numeric example in the design doc.
Alyssa Chen: Added hard cap (15% of pool) and example workload calculation in docs/design/diffusive-reservation.md; also added unit test for cap enforcement.
Leah Ortiz: Telemetry cardinality looks high — can we aggregate fingerprints server-side to avoid high-cardinality labels?

Alyssa Chen: Fingerprints are exported as a single compact sketch ID (128-bit) and we added sampling + rollup in pkg/telemetry to avoid high cardinality. Documented in telemetry file and added integration test.
Samir Patel: Did you run the canary with heterogeneous GPU types? We need to ensure cross-instance fairness.

Alyssa Chen: Canary run included mixed GPU pools (A100/V100). Added per-instance normalization and a small translation table in allocator to account for throughput delta; results added to bench output.
